newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Prudential moves ScotAm fund to London.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Prudential moves ScotAm fund to London.

text.p: British insurance giant Prudential Corp said on Monday it will transfer management of Scottish Amicable's 15 billion pounds ($25 billion) of policyholder funds from Glasgow to its London-based Prudential Portfolio Management (PPM).

The move follows the 2.8 billion pound acquisition of the Scottish mutual insurer in March and is likely once again to stir sensitivities about the future of Scotland's independent financial community.
Perth-based insurer General Accident caused a row last October when it announced it was moving the bulk of its fund management activities to London.

Job losses and the possible impact on the Scottish financial sector were contentious issues during the battle for control of ScotAm and the Pru's winning bid included guarantees that job levels at its Craigforth headquarters near Stirling would be maintained for three years.
Those assurances, however, did not include the investment mangement business nor its 125 employees.
The Scotam operation is dwarfed by the Pru's own fund management subsidiary which employs around 1,100 fund managers and support staff in nine offices worldwide.
At the end of 1996, PPM had 91 billion pounds under management.

The Pru had said it would consider the possibility of continuing a fund mangement activity in Glasgow but Derek Higgs, chairman of PPM said it had since concluded it was not "economically supportable" for ScotAm's investment business to continue in its present form.
Nor was there a basis for locating particular investment functions of an enlarged PPM in Glasgow, he added.
ScotAm managing director Roy Nicolson said he regretted that the fund management operation could not have been retained in Glasgow.
"However, it was not viable to do so and therefore not in our policyholders interests," he said.

Disappointment at the loss of the ScotAm funds from Scotland may be tempered by news that Britannia Investment Managers' had acquired ScotAm's 800 million pound third party institutional funds for an undisclosed sum.
As part of the agreement Douglas Ferrans, chief executive of Scotam's investment management operation and sixteen other employees will join Britannia.

The Pru said it would be discussing work opportunities in London with other professional staff at thge investment management operation and had guaranteed jobs to the balance of back office staff until the end of the year.
It said it hoped there would be no compulsory lay-offs as a result of today's move.
The formal transfer of management of Scottish Amicable's investments to PPM takes place on September 30 subject to court and regulatory approval of the takeover. ($ = 0.591 British Pounds)
